title: Negationism in India: Concealing the Record of Islam
byline: by Koenraad Elst · Voice of India · 1992, enlarged 1993
lede: In Europe, “negationism” means denying the Holocaust. Elst, a Belgian, applies the word to India. His charge is that since about 1920, Indian politicians, Muslim apologists and Marxist historians have denied or played down centuries of persecution of Hindus under Muslim rule, and that the Indian establishment backs this denial. The book grew from a 1992 article in a Flemish Catholic monthly and a review of Sita Ram Goel's Hindu Temples, Vol. 2.
facts: chapters: negationism in general, in India, its refutation, and replies to critics
when Elst dates its start, in the Congress–Khilafat alliance
kinds of negationism he compares: of the Holocaust, of the Armenian genocide, and of Islam's record in India
India became the first country to ban The Satanic Verses, which he cites as a symptom
note: Elst's comparison of Indian historiography with Holocaust denial is deliberately provocative and is rejected by the historians he names. They argue they are interpreting the evidence, not denying it. This page sets out his argument, attributed to him.
